bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: R CMD check warns about links to separate package's index

comments.text:
My goal here is to allow for a link to a separate package's help index -- for example, the `stats` package's help index. This works:

    \link[stats:00Index]{Link to 'stats' package help index}

but R CMD check gives the warning:

    * checking Rd cross-references ... WARNING
Missing link or links in documentation object 'hello.Rd':
  '[stats:00Index]{This index}'
comments.creator: kevinushey

comments.text:
Sorry, additional comments got lost; in addition the text doesn't match in the original comment. Forgive the redundancy but I believe it's more 'polite' to submit a more full-fledged bug report as a second comment.

Given the line in a .Rd page:

    \link[stats:00Index]{stats help}

A link to the stats help index is properly generated, but R CMD check warns:

    * checking Rd cross-references ... WARNING
    Missing link or links in documentation object 'hello.Rd':
      '[stats:00Index]{stats help}'


I did not see any relevant text in R-exts (http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Cross_002dreferences); in case there is a different, proper method of linking to another package's help index.

Is this a bug in R CMD check, or is there an alternative method for linking to a package's help index?

I'm using R version 3.2.0 Patched (2015-04-26 r68264) -- "Full of Ingredients"

Thanks,
Kevin
comments.creator: kevinushey
elin.waring
comments.text:
I found a discussion of this question on StackOverflow circa 2022.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70654391/r-package-documentation-link-to-a-whole-package-not-function

Basically, whether and how to do this will depend on whether the package maintainer has created an index page and also whether you want hyperlinks.
